newsitem.title: EGYPT: Apache wells in Egypt test at 9,205 bpd.
newsitem.headline: Apache wells in Egypt test at 9,205 bpd.

text.p: Apache Corp and its partners in Egypt said in a statement on Thursday that they completed two oil discoveries on the Khalda concession in Egypt's Western desert that tested a combined 9,205 barrels a day.
They said in a statement they marked the first oil production from the Kenz field.

The Kenz-5X and Kenz-6 each discovered new oil reservoirs and extended the boundaries of Kenz fields. Results from the wells generated three other locations in the Kenz field area to be drilled during the rest of the year, the statement said.

"As we're finding in fields throughout the Khalda concession, Kenz field is bigger and more complex than previously believed. With each well drilled, we're discovering new oil reserves in formations that previously produced only gas and finding new pay zones that add to our portfolio of drilling opportunities in the area," said Apache President and Chief Operating Officer G. Steven Farris.
Kenz-6 flowed at 5,900 bpd and 16 million cubic feet of gas from a new pay zone. It was perforated at a depth of approximately 9,000 feet.
The well logged 248 feet of net pay from a total of seven reservoirs. It is currently producing into nearby production facilities at a restricted rate of 2,000 bpd.

The Kenz-5X discovery well initial daily production rate was 3,305 bpd and 435,000 cubic feet of gas. The well penetrated a total of 142 feet of net pay, and is currently producing at a restricted rate of approximately 1,100 bpd.

Three oil bearing and four gas bearing reservoirs also have been identified in the well. The gas-bearing zones in both the Kenz-5X and Kenz-6 will be produced subsequent to the construction of a natural gas pipeline.
Apache owns 40 percent of the contractor interest in the Khalda concession. Repsol SA of Spain is the operator of the group and owns 50 percent. Samsung Co owns ten percent.
The Khalda Petroleum Co is the Egyptian corporation which operates the concessions. It is held by the partners and the Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation.
